description: Fetch full curated UniProtKB entries by accession in one batch of up to 20 distinct accessions; repeats collapse, and any further accessions return in deferredAccessions to pass as accessions on the next call. Each entry carries alternative names, function, EC numbers and catalytic activity, cofactors, biophysicochemical properties (enzyme kinetics, pH and temperature dependence, redox potential, absorption), active and binding sites with their ligands, subcellular location and membrane topology, disease involvement, PTMs, molecule processing (signal, propeptides, chains), natural variants, isoforms, domains, free-text comments (PTM, pathway, subunit, tissue specificity), GO terms with their evidence, keywords, cross-references, and Ensembl gene IDs; mutagenesis and IntAct interaction partners come back when sections or fields name them. Partial failures do not abort the batch — resolved entries land in succeeded[] and unknown or inactive (merged, demerged, deleted) accessions in failed[], where an inactive accession names its replacement or UniParc ID. Pass fields to trim the upstream projection; a field this tool cannot return (e.g. sequence) is not requested and is listed in ignoredFields with a notice. Each record is measured on its own across both output surfaces: one within 24,000 UTF-8 bytes returns in succeeded[]; a larger one is listed in outlinedEntries with its size instead. Re-call an outlined accession alone, e.g. accessions:["P04637"], for its section outline (kind: "outline", sections with byte sizes), then add sections:["disease","variants"] to select sections. sections takes exactly one accession; trim a batch with fields instead. All returned list items and cross-reference IDs render in full. A large list section pages with section_limit/section_offset on a re-call naming that one section. To see what is annotated at one residue, pass residue with one accession, e.g. accessions:["P04637"], residue:175, sections:["variants","domains"]: each position-bearing section keeps only its rows covering that canonical position, and residueCoverage counts the covered, excluded, and total rows per section. This tool does not search: accessions come from uniprot_search_proteins.results[].accession or uniprot_map_ids. Strip any isoform suffix (P04637-2 to P04637) before calling.

accessions.description: Accessions to fetch (1–500). Repeats collapse to their first occurrence; the first 20 distinct are fetched and the rest return in deferredAccessions, in order, for the next call. From uniprot_search_proteins or uniprot_map_ids.

items.description: A UniProtKB primary accession, e.g. "P04637". Canonical form only — strip any "-N" isoform suffix.

fields.description: Comma-separated UniProtKB return-field names to fetch in place of the default record, e.g. "accession,cc_function,ft_variant,xref_pdb" — trims a batch. Omit for the default record. The identity fields always come back. Names are case-insensitive; keywordid is sent as keyword and rhea as cc_catalytic_activity. Any xref_ field (e.g. xref_reactome) fills xrefs. A field this tool does not return (e.g. sequence, which uniprot_get_sequence returns, or ft_helix) is not requested from UniProt and comes back in ignoredFields with a notice listing the supported fields. An xref_ database UniProt does not know, or text that is not a field name, fails invalid_fields with UniProt's message.

residue.description: A residue position, 1-based on the canonical sequence, e.g. 175. Keeps only the rows covering it in each position-bearing section — sites, topology, ptms, processing, variants, mutagenesis, domains — in UniProt order: a disulfide bond or cross-link covers its two bonded residues; any other row covers start through end, an OUTSIDE or UNSURE bound counting at its value. A row numbered on an isoform, a non-bond row with an UNKNOWN bound, or a bond with no known partner never matches and is counted as excluded. A section with no covering row is left out; residueCoverage gives each section's covered, excluded, and total rows. Other sections return as usual; with sections, only the named ones are filtered and returned. Filtering comes before section_limit/section_offset and the 24,000-byte check, so windows, totalCount, nextOffset, and outline sizes count covering rows — keep residue on every re-call. Requires exactly one accession; a residue past the entry's length fails.

section_limit.description: Window size for one list section on a sections re-call: return at most this many items of it (at least 1; a value past the remaining items returns them all). Requires sections naming exactly one list section, e.g. ["variants"] (or ptms, domains, goTerms). Omit together with section_offset to return the whole section.

section_offset.description: Zero-based index of the first item in the windowed section. Defaults to 0. Pass the previous response's nextOffset to page forward, keeping residue when it was set. Same requirements as section_limit; set without section_limit, returns every item from this index on.

sections.description: Section keys to return for one accession, e.g. ["disease","variants"]: the record is cut to these plus its identity fields. Re-call an accession with it after a kind: "outline" response, or name the on-request sections mutagenesis and interactions, which the default record leaves out — without fields, naming one fetches it; with fields, include ft_mutagen or cc_interaction there. Requires exactly one accession: a batch with sections is rejected, so trim a batch with fields. A requested section the record lacks is named in absentSections, not an error.

items.description: A section key of the entry record, e.g. "disease", "variants", "mutagenesis", "interactions". Case-insensitive.

name: uniprot_get_entry

absentSections.description: Requested section keys this record does not carry — UniProt holds no annotation of that kind for it, or fields excluded it. Not an error: the other requested sections are returned. Present only on a sections re-call that named one.

items.description: A requested section key the record does not carry.

cap.description: The section_limit applied. Present when truncated.

deferredAccessions.description: Distinct accessions past the first 20, in submission order — not fetched. Pass them as accessions on the next call, which fetches their first 20 and defers the rest again. Absent when nothing was deferred.

items.description: A submitted accession this call did not fetch.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `sections_single_accession`: sections was passed with more than one submitted accession (a repeat counts) — rejected before any request. sections re-calls a single outlined record. `unknown_section`: sections named a key this tool never emits — rejected before any request. The message lists every valid key. `invalid_section_window`: section_limit or section_offset was set without sections naming exactly one list section — no sections, several, or a non-list section such as organism or xrefs. Rejected before any request. `all_not_found`: None of the fetched accessions resolved to an active entry — each was unknown to UniProtKB or inactive (merged, demerged, or deleted) — and none was deferred. The message names each inactive accession and its replacement. `invalid_fields`: UniProtKB rejected the fields value — the message relays UniProt naming the rejected field. `residue_single_accession`: residue was passed with more than one submitted accession (a repeat counts) — rejected before any request. residue cuts one record. `residue_out_of_range`: residue is past the end of the entry's canonical sequence. Raised once the accession resolves; the message names the canonical length. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

failed.description: Accessions that did not resolve to an active entry — unknown to UniProtKB, or inactive (merged, demerged, or deleted) — in request order.

accession.description: The requested accession that did not resolve.

error.description: Why it failed and how to recover. For an inactive accession: the merge target to retry with, the demerge products to choose among, or the UniParc ID that keeps a deleted sequence.

ignoredFields.description: Names in fields this tool does not return, in request order — left out of the UniProt request, so the call answered without them. Absent when every name was returned.

items.description: A requested field name, lowercased, that this tool does not return.

kind.description: Result kind. "full": read succeeded[], failed[], and any outlinedEntries and deferredAccessions — every call with more than one distinct accession or any failure. "outline": a lone accession whose record alone (cut to the rows covering residue, when set) exceeded 24,000 UTF-8 bytes; read sections and re-call it with sections:[...].

nextOffset.description: section_offset for the next window (same section_limit, and the same residue when set). Present while items remain.

notice.description: Re-call guidance. On a single-record outline: re-call that accession with sections:[...] (and the same residue, when set) to pull specific sections. When outlinedEntries is present: re-call each listed accession alone. When deferredAccessions is present: pass them as accessions on the next call. On a section window: the section_offset that pages the rest, or why the window came back empty. When ignoredFields is present: the ignored fields, where to get them, and the fields this tool returns.

outlinedEntries.description: Resolved entries whose one-accession result alone exceeds 24,000 UTF-8 bytes, in request order — not inlined. Re-call each alone for its section outline. Absent when every resolved record fits.

items.description: A resolved entry too large to inline, and its size.

accession.description: Accession to re-call alone with accessions:[accession].

bytes.description: UTF-8 bytes of this record returned alone, across both output surfaces — the measure the 24,000-byte budget compares.

residue.description: The residue the position-bearing sections were cut to, 1-based on the canonical sequence — the residue input. Present only when residue was set; residueCoverage gives each section its covered, excluded, and total rows.

residueCoverage.description: How the residue input cut the record: for each position-bearing section the record carried (only the named ones, with sections), the rows covering the residue, the rows that could not be placed on the canonical sequence, and the rows before the filter. A section listed with covered 0 is left out of the record. Present only when residue was set, on full and outline results.

residue.description: The residue the sections were cut to, as passed.

sections.description: One row per position-bearing section filtered, in record order. Empty when the record (or the sections named) carries none.

covered.description: Rows covering the residue — the rows the record keeps for this section.

excluded.description: Rows the rule cannot place on the canonical sequence — numbered on an isoform, a non-bond row with an UNKNOWN bound, or a bond with no known partner. Never kept, so read this before concluding nothing is annotated at the residue.

total.description: The section's rows before the filter.

sections.description: Section outline for a lone accession whose record alone exceeds the 24,000-byte budget. A batch lists such records in outlinedEntries instead.

items.description: An outlined section with its serialized size.

bytes.description: Serialized byte size of the section — of its rows covering residue, when set.

name.description: Section identifier — pass a subset in sections:[...] to retrieve it.

shown.description: Items in the returned window. Present when truncated.

succeeded.description: Entries that resolved and fit the 24,000-byte per-record budget, in request order. Present when kind is "full"; empty when none did.

alternativeNames.description: Alternative full protein names. Absent when none.

biophysicochemical.description: Biophysicochemical properties: enzyme kinetics (KM, Vmax, kcat notes), pH and temperature dependence, redox potential, and absorption, one object per comment, each value with its own evidence. The fields kinetics, ph_dependence, temp_dependence, redox_potential, and absorption each return the whole comment. Absent when none are annotated.
